sar.narrative:
In the case identified as HHG-006, suspicious activity was detected involving a transaction of $482.12, significantly higher than the account holder's average spending of $118.56. The account holder explicitly disputed this transaction, asserting they did not authorize it. This transaction was executed using a device identified as 'New' to the account, suggesting potential use of a new or stolen device. Notably, this particular device profile has been associated with 20 previous fraud cases, including cases labeled 'CC-0570', 'CC-0779', and 'CC-1017,' indicating a pattern of fraudulent activity.

The suspect transaction is part of a series of four online purchases completed within a 30-minute window, all of which were made using a device previously unseen by this account. This scenario matches the pattern for card-not-present incidents associated with a new device, raising suspicions of deliberate manipulation. Further investigation reveals the same device profile is linked to 30 different cards, many connected to confirmed fraud cases, suggesting its involvement in a sophisticated fraud ring.

The coincidence of multiple high-value, rapid transactions deviating from the customer's typical spending behavior, combined with the customer's own report of unauthorized activity, strengthens the suspicion of a compromised card. All indicators point to card C07297-K1 being caught in a broader device-based fraud operation.
